reviewer: Independent reviewer (Claude Opus 5 CLI documentation review seat)

fixture.providerMode: dedicated local OpenID Connect fixture; full browser authorization and callback; no external identity-provider account

steps.action: A Business User on an allowed domain enters the Portal with a magic link
steps.actual: Hannah Blum, on the allowed domain northwind.example, requested a link from the Legal request portal, saw the neutral "Check your email" response, and the emailed link opened the Portal under her identity. She was never invited: Portal entry created the account.

steps.action: An address outside the allowed domains gets the same neutral answer and no link
steps.actual: rio.santos@blackpine.example, on no allowed domain, saw the identical "Check your email" screen but no message arrived within 7 seconds and no account was created. The neutral response does not confirm eligibility, which is why the guide tells an Administrator to confirm an unapproved address cannot establish a new account rather than trusting the screen.

steps.action: The Business User appears in Users and cannot be given a staff role by invitation
steps.actual: The Portal-created account is listed in Settings then Users with role Business user. A staff invitation for the same address was refused with "This user already exists with a different role." and sent no email, confirming the corrected guide: a Business User address cannot be converted to staff through the invitation form.

steps.action: The Users table Role control offers four choices and promotes a Business User in place
steps.actual: The Users table Role control is a menu offering four choices, Administrator, Legal team member, Contributor and Business user, one more than the invitation form. Choosing Contributor promoted the Portal-created account to staff in place, which is the capability the corrected guide now records.

steps.action: Promoting a Portal-created account turns its row into a pending invitation without a Role control
steps.actual: After the in-place promotion from Business user to Contributor, the row reads Contributor and Invited, and its Role control is gone. Only Resend invite and Revoke invite remain; there is no Archive control either. A Portal-created account has never set a password, so promoting it leaves a pending staff invitation, and the role cannot be changed again from the table until it activates.

steps.action: The promoted person activates through Resend invite and the row becomes Active
steps.actual: Resend invite delivered a set-password link to the promoted account. After setting a password the row moved to Active, which is the recovery path back to a manageable staff row.

steps.action: With the row Active again, the Role control returns and offers all four roles
steps.actual: Once the account was Active the Role control reappeared with all four choices, Administrator, Legal team member, Contributor and Business user, and choosing Business user returned it to Portal-only access. So the fourth choice does return a staff account to the Portal, but only while the row is Active.
